title: Rigveda 9.22: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.22: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.22 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 676v-677r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.22.1-6 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 676v
translation.original_text:
1e̱te somā̍sa ā̱śavo̱ rathā̍ iva̱ pra vā̱jina̍ḥ | sargā̍ḥ sṛ̱ṣṭā a̍heṣata ||
2e̱te vātā̍ ivo̱rava̍ḥ pa̱rjanya̍syeva vṛ̱ṣṭaya̍ḥ | a̱gner i̍va bhra̱mā vṛthā̍ ||
3e̱te pū̱tā vi̍pa̱ścita̱ḥ somā̍so̱ dadhyā̍śiraḥ | vi̱pā vy ā̍naśu̱r dhiya̍ḥ ||
4e̱te mṛ̱ṣṭā ama̍rtyāḥ sasṛ̱vāṁso̱ na śa̍śramuḥ | iya̍kṣantaḥ pa̱tho raja̍ḥ ||
5e̱te pṛ̱ṣṭhāni̱ roda̍sor vipra̱yanto̱ vy ā̍naśuḥ | u̱tedam u̍tta̱maṁ raja̍ḥ ||
6tantu̍ṁ tanvā̱nam u̍tta̱mam anu̍ pra̱vata̍ āśata | u̱tedam u̍tta̱māyya̍m ||
translation.text:
1THESE rapid Soma-streams have stirred themselves to motion like strong steeds, Like cars, like armies hurried forth.
2Swift as wide winds they lightly move, like rain-storms of Parjanya, like The flickering flames of burning fire.
3These Soma juices, blent with curds, purified, skilled in sacred hymns, Have gained by song their hearts'desire.
4Immortal, cleansed, these drops, since first they flowed, have never wearied, fain To reach the regions and their paths.
5Advancing they have travelled o'er the ridges of the earth and heaven, And this the highest realm of all.
6Over the heights have they attained the highest thread that is spun out, And this which must be deemed most high.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 676v (numbered 98v by the scribe) (OPenn image 677, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.21.4 ‹-pavamānāsaḥ āśata hitāḥ na›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 677r (numbered 99r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.22.7 ‹gavyāni dhārayaḥ tatam tantum›. Verses 9.22.1-6 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 9.22.7 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 677r
translation.original_text: <sup>7</sup>tvaṁ so̍ma pa̱ṇibhya̱ ā vasu̱ gavyā̍ni dhārayaḥ | ta̱taṁ tantu̍m acikradaḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>7</sup>Thou, Soma, boldest wealth in kine which thou hast seized from niggard churls: Thou calledst forth the outspun thread.
